items.title: Search command catalog covers seven distinct interactions
items.statement: The first segment wires find-in-files, next, open, previous, rebuild-index, replace-all, and replace-in-files commands from named Search-surface elements to named search handlers.
items.impact: The command inventory and direct UI-to-handler ownership are explicit for this window.

items.title: Search, settings, and sound command catalog covers seven interactions
items.statement: The second segment wires replace-selected, set-scope, show-search, a dry-method-default-guard setting update, notification settings open, sound-asset delete, and sound-asset export.
items.impact: The heterogeneous command inventory and handler targets are explicit for this window.

items.title: Sound and source-control command catalog covers seven interactions
items.statement: The third segment wires sound restore, mapping set, pack import, preview, upload, source-control commit-group acceptance, and commit-message generation.
items.impact: The command inventory and handler ownership are explicit for this window.

items.title: Source-control graph, history, and conflict catalog covers seven interactions
items.statement: The fourth segment wires compatibility and canonical graph-filter/focus commands, graph layout, history commit open, and conflict-resolved marking.
items.impact: The catalog exposes both compatibility lineage and canonical command authority in this window.

items.title: Source-control conflict and review catalog covers seven interactions
items.statement: The fifth segment wires open-conflict, open-merge-editor, open-review, resolve-conflict-side, review-filter, review-open, and review-swap commands.
items.impact: The conflict and review command inventory and handler targets are explicit for this window.

items.title: Dispatcher and correlation behavior is consistently required
items.statement: Every reviewed row requires dispatcher registration with typed arguments/results and dispatch evidence carrying command identity, origin, correlation identity, handler target, result, and an effect receipt or event.
items.impact: The matrix establishes a common traceable dispatch envelope rather than permitting direct untracked UI calls.

evidence.exact_quote: "cmd.search.find_in_files dispatch evidence must preserve command_id, origin, correlation_id, handler target, result, and receipt or event effect",
"cmd.source_control.review.swap dispatch evidence must preserve command_id, origin, correlation_id, handler target, result, and receipt or event effect",

items.title: Typed payload and result contracts are required but not defined
items.statement: The rows repeatedly require a typed payload/result contract, but this excerpt provides no type names, fields, validation rules, success variants, error variants, versioning rules, or serialization boundaries for any of the 35 commands.
items.impact: Independent builders can produce incompatible command shapes while each claiming to satisfy the abstract typed-contract requirement; fixtures cannot falsify semantic incompatibility.

items.title: Pre-dispatch availability and disabled-reason projections are explicit
items.statement: Each command declares a projected availability selector and a separate disabled-reason projection, and accessibility contracts require unavailable reasons to reach assistive technology.
items.impact: Controls have an explicit source for enablement and explanatory unavailable copy.

evidence.exact_quote: "disabled_announcement": "catalog.search_find_in_files surfaces state.commands.search_find_in_files.disabled_reason to assistive technology when unavailable."

items.title: Command lifecycle states stop at pre-dispatch availability
items.statement: The common state model names availability and disabled reason before dispatch but no queued, running, progress, cancelling, succeeded, partially-succeeded, failed, retryable, stale, or rolled-back projections, nor any rule binding correlation_id to those GUI states.
items.impact: Long-running, remote, or mutating commands can remain enabled, display stale success, or lose partial-failure and cancellation truth.

evidence.exact_quote: "cmd.search.rebuild_index must expose projected state selector and disabled reason before dispatch",
"focus_management": "catalog.source_control_review_open preserves visible focus and returns focus deterministically after dispatch or error."

items.title: Command controls have a four-part accessibility baseline
items.statement: Every reviewed control requires stable role/name/description semantics, keyboard reachability and activation, visible deterministic focus handling after dispatch or error, and disabled-state announcement.
items.impact: The matrix does not permit mouse-only controls or silent disabled states.

evidence.exact_quote: "role_or_semantics": "catalog.search_open_result exposes a stable role/name/description matching cmd.search.open_result."
"keyboard_access": "catalog.search_open_result is reachable and activatable by keyboard where the control is visible."
"focus_management": "catalog.search_open_result preserves visible focus and returns focus deterministically after dispatch or error."
"disabled_announcement": "catalog.search_open_result surfaces state.commands.search_open_result.disabled_reason to assistive technology when unavailable."

items.title: Every command has named dispatcher, projection, effect, and accessibility evidence
items.statement: The common acceptance pattern supplies named dispatcher fixtures, projected-state assertions, receipt/event assertions, accessibility regressions, and event-specific checks where events are declared.
items.impact: Production certification has a concrete minimum evidence inventory rather than an untestable prose-only assertion.

items.title: Certification oracles omit semantic end states and adversarial failures
items.statement: The named evidence proves dispatch reachability, selector reads, generic receipt/event presence, and control accessibility, but does not require semantic result assertions, invalid input, permission denial, concurrent mutation, cancellation, crash recovery, rollback, offline, scale, or security abuse tests.
items.impact: A command can satisfy every listed fixture while producing the wrong files, repository state, settings value, remote view, or recovery behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: "requirement": "Dispatching cmd.sound.asset.delete reaches handlers::sound::asset_delete with typed args/result contract."
"requirement": "cmd.sound.asset.delete has no declared persisted event; dispatch must still record a no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition."

items.title: Execution targets are named but authority boundaries are absent
items.statement: Handler locations identify execution ownership, but the rows do not define which principals may delete assets, change agent defaults, accept commit groups, mutate conflicts, access remote reviews, or select filesystem destinations, nor how workspace trust and repository scope constrain them.
items.impact: UI availability can be mistaken for authorization, and handlers may operate outside the intended workspace, repository, provider account, or user capability.

items.title: Receipt, event, and projection consumers are not named
items.statement: Rows name a UI element, handler, state path, and receipt/event reference, but do not identify the projector that owns availability/disabled reason, the receipt store and retention owner, event consumers, retry/replay consumers, or which views refresh after effects.
items.impact: A handler may complete without the appropriate search, sound, settings, graph, conflict, or review surface being invalidated and refreshed.

items.title: Error, retry, cancellation, partial failure, and rollback contracts are absent
items.statement: The excerpt mentions returning focus after an error, but defines no error taxonomy, user-visible remediation, retryability, idempotency key, cancellation point, partial-success accounting, cleanup, restart recovery, compensation, or rollback for any command.
items.impact: Mutating and long-running operations can leave partial files, repository state, imported assets, settings, or remote views without deterministic recovery.

"cmd.search.replace_in_files has no declared persisted event; dispatch must still record a no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition."

items.title: Mutating search commands are classified as no-persist receipts
items.statement: Rebuild-index, replace-all, and replace-in-files declare no expected event and require no-persist receipts, even though their names imply durable index or file changes; no changed-file set, preimage/version guard, atomicity, undo, rollback, or postcondition event is specified.
items.impact: File or index mutation may be invisible to projectors and audit history, race stale search results, and become impossible to recover after partial application.

items.title: Search semantics and hostile workspace inputs are unspecified
items.statement: Find/open/next/previous/replace rows do not define query syntax, regex and replacement escaping, case/word flags, scope and exclusion grammar, symlink policy, binary and encoding behavior, result ordering, end-of-list wrap, stale-result handling, maximum files/results, catastrophic-regex protection, or cancellation on large workspaces.
items.impact: Builders can disagree on matches and replacements, hang on adversarial patterns, traverse unintended files, or open a result whose file/range changed after search.

items.title: Opening notification settings is modeled as settings mutation
items.statement: cmd.settings.open_notifications is an Open Notifications navigation command yet declares settings.updated and must emit it, conflating view opening with a durable settings update.
items.impact: Opening a panel can spuriously dirty settings, trigger persistence or synchronization consumers, and produce misleading audit history.

evidence.exact_quote: "Assert cmd.settings.open_notifications emits expected event type settings.updated with command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target."

items.title: Agent-rule setting update event is too generic to reconstruct or arbitrate
items.statement: The dry-method-default-guard setter emits only settings.updated; the excerpt does not bind the event to setting key, old/new value, scope, actor authority, schema version, validation result, revision precondition, persistence completion, or rollback.
items.impact: Consumers cannot deterministically project the setting, detect lost updates, audit what changed, or restore the prior value.

items.title: Sound asset delete and export omit destructive and filesystem semantics
items.statement: Delete has no event, confirmation, reference-impact check, trash/undo, retention, or concurrent-use rule; export has no destination capability, format, overwrite/collision, path-sandbox, atomic-write, permission-denial, cancellation, or partial-file cleanup contract.
items.impact: Delete can orphan mappings or irreversibly remove content, while export can overwrite arbitrary files or leave corrupt partial output.

items.statement: Asset restore, mapping set, pack import, and upload each declare no expected event and explicitly use no-persist receipts despite command names that imply durable catalog, mapping, storage, or remote-state changes.
items.impact: Sound inventories and mappings may change without authoritative projection invalidation, audit reconstruction, synchronization, or recovery signals.

items.statement: Import and upload do not specify accepted formats/codecs, MIME and magic-byte validation, archive path traversal, decompression ratios, file and aggregate size limits, duplicate naming, metadata sanitization, malware policy, temporary storage, progress, cancellation, network loss, retries, resumability, or cleanup.
items.impact: A malicious or oversized pack can escape its destination, exhaust disk or memory, persist unsafe metadata, or leave orphaned local/remote content after failure.

items.title: Sound preview has no playback state or device-failure contract
items.statement: Preview is receipt-only and defines no selected asset/version, start/stop/toggle behavior, one-at-a-time rule, seek/volume semantics, audio-device change or loss, decode failure, duration limit, resource release, or accessible non-audio status.
items.impact: Repeated previews can overlap or leak resources, and the UI cannot reliably report playing, stopped, or failed state to all users.

items.statement: The command is receipt-only and explicitly forbids placeholder events, but it does not define commit-group identity, exact accepted effect, repository and branch preconditions, clean/dirty worktree rules, user authority, stale-head detection, atomicity, idempotency, conflict handling, or rollback.
items.impact: A stale or unauthorized acceptance can mutate the wrong repository state without a replayable event or a defined recovery path.

items.title: Commit-message generation lacks provider, privacy, and adversarial-content rules
items.statement: The generator contract does not specify which repository data is collected, secret/redaction policy, user consent and preview, provider/model authority, retention, prompt-injection treatment of diff text, maximum context, deterministic fallback, cancellation, rate limiting, network loss, or whether generated text is merely returned or applied.
items.impact: Sensitive diffs can leave the machine without a defined boundary, hostile repository text can steer generation, and offline/provider failure has no safe UI outcome.

items.title: Graph filter, focus, and layout omit large-repository and stale-data behavior
items.statement: Graph commands do not define filter grammar, focus target identity, layout modes, ordering stability, maximum nodes/edges, incremental or virtualized rendering, cancellation, cache invalidation, concurrent repository changes, missing objects, or how focus is preserved when filtering removes the focused node.
items.impact: Large or changing histories can freeze the interface, produce nondeterministic layouts, or show a focused commit that is no longer in the filtered graph.

items.title: Open-commit lacks commit-reference validation and unavailable-object behavior
items.statement: The history-open command does not define the commit identifier form, repository binding, rev-parse ambiguity policy, abbreviated-hash collisions, missing or shallow-clone object behavior, replaced history, path safety for displayed content, concurrent repository changes, or offline fetch policy.
items.impact: A stale or ambiguous reference can open the wrong commit, trigger unintended resolution behavior, or fail without a deterministic user-visible state.

items.title: Mark-conflict-resolved can race worktree content and has no durable effect
items.statement: Marking a conflict resolved is receipt-only and does not require conflict-marker validation, stage/index postconditions, file identity or content hash preconditions, unsaved-buffer coordination, submodule/binary/rename cases, atomic staging, concurrent-change rejection, or rollback.
items.impact: The command can stage stale or still-conflicted content, overwrite newer edits, and leave source-control projections inconsistent without an authoritative event.

items.title: Overlapping source-control open commands lack canonical ownership
items.statement: open_conflict and open_merge_editor both target conflict UI territory, while cmd.source_control.open_review and cmd.source_control.review.open are separate commands with separate handlers and state paths; no alias, specialization, routing, or mutual-exclusion rule explains the distinctions.
items.impact: Different callers can open divergent surfaces for the same intent, and future compatibility migration has no declared canonical command.

items.title: Resolve-conflict-side lacks a safe destructive transition contract
items.statement: The row does not define the side enum and meaning across merge/rebase, target file and conflict-hunk identity, base/ours/theirs version hashes, dirty-buffer confirmation, mixed-resolution handling, binary and rename cases, atomic write/stage behavior, undo snapshot, concurrent edit rejection, or rollback; it is also receipt-only.
items.impact: A stale or ambiguous side selection can discard user changes or resolve the wrong conflict without an authoritative transition record or recovery route.

items.title: Review commands omit remote authority, network, and stale-data behavior
items.statement: Review open/filter/swap contracts do not define provider/repository/review identity, account and permission checks, token expiry, pagination, rate limits, server-side versus local filtering, base/head freshness, force-push handling, cached/offline behavior, retry/backoff, cancellation, or which remote data may be retained locally.
items.impact: The UI can show stale or unauthorized review data as current, mishandle expired credentials and force pushes, or leak provider data through undefined caching.

items.title: Review filter and swap semantics are not falsifiable

items.impact: Receipts may be too weak for support or too rich for privacy, grow without bound, and expose sensitive workspace or provider content.

items.title: Generic control accessibility does not cover dynamic content or localization
items.statement: Stable role/name, keyboard activation, focus return, and disabled announcement are valuable, but the rows do not define localized message keys and parameterization, live-region behavior for progress/results/errors, result-list and graph navigation semantics, merge-editor reading order, side labels, audio preview alternatives, truncation/overflow, or right-to-left behavior.
items.impact: Controls may technically pass the listed fixture while dynamic search, graph, audio, conflict, and review experiences remain unusable or untranslated.

items.title: Durable-effect classification cannot be resolved inside this excerpt
items.statement: It is unknown whether search, sound, and source-control mutations are intentionally modeled as external/non-domain side effects elsewhere, or whether their empty expected_event_types arrays are omissions; the excerpt supplies no cross-document effect taxonomy or referenced owner contract that resolves the classification.
items.impact: Production certification cannot safely infer that receipt-only is correct for durable mutations without adjudicating the owning event and persistence contracts.

items.impact: No implementation or production-readiness conclusion can be drawn from these contract rows alone.

highest_risk_themes: Commands that appear to mutate files, sound catalogs, mappings, repository state, or conflicts are modeled as no-persist receipts without authoritative domain transitions.
Typed inputs/results are asserted but not defined, leaving core behavior, validation, errors, and versioning to incompatible builder inference.
Long-running and remote operations lack lifecycle, cancellation, partial-failure, rollback, offline, stale-data, and GUI-truth contracts.
Sound import/upload and commit-message generation lack explicit untrusted-input, privacy, data-lifecycle, and resource-limit boundaries.
Compatibility and command-namespace seams create duplicate authority and evidence ambiguity for graph and review/open commands.
synthesis.certification_implication: The rows provide a strong common wiring-evidence scaffold, but this excerpt alone is insufficient for production certification until durable-effect classification, concrete payload/result schemas, lifecycle/recovery states, authority/security boundaries, semantic end-state oracles, and the identified namespace contradictions are adjudicated.
